notes.title: Update 1.1.0
notes.content: [h3]Hey everyone![/h3][p]We’ve got a lot to share today, so grab a snack.[/p][p][/p][h2]Soundtrack Release[/h2][p]The Official SkullX: Aibohphobia OST is out![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/e9015d894fc9223cd57c94d5eee881abe7a45959.png"][/img]17 instrumental tracks—50 minutes of gloom, despair, and a dash of electrochemical shock courtesy of our Mysterious Wanderer—all composed by the talented [b]Arthur Farrakhov[/b]. [/p][p]You can check it out right now on [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3958130/SkullX_Aibohphobia__Official_Soundtrack/"]Steam[/url], [url="https://open.spotify.com/album/2gyANgtzIFp6hJhK2uekDD?si=D3i67jGhSeu7e0uFK2lPQw"]Spotify[/url] and all major streaming platforms.[/p][p][/p][h2]Chinese Localization[/h2][p]We’re excited to announce that SkullX is now fully localized in Simplified Chinese![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/9745e1da73afe2a82b937a6316f33aa3f51ac2b3.png"][/img]Huge thanks to our translation partners [b]WeMavin Languages[/b] who wrestled with BBCode monsters and occult riddles to make this possible.[/p][p][/p][h2]Writing Updates[/h2][p]We’ve combed through community feedback and made a round of text and writing edits across the game.[/p][p]Nothing major was rewritten — but certain scenes are now sharper, smoother, and closer to the tone we always wanted.[/p][p][/p][h2]What’s Next in Localization[/h2][p]We’re not stopping with Chinese. [b]Russian[/b], [b]French[/b], and [b]Polish[/b] localizations are already in the works.[/p][p]We’ll share progress updates as we go — and yes, Russian is being handled in-house by our writer.[/p][p][/p][h3]That’s the news for now.[/h3][p]As always, [b]thank you[/b] for playing, sharing, reviewing, and generally being the fuel that keeps our merc squad alive! [/p][p]Keep your eyes peeled — [b]release date for Chapter 2 will be revealed soon[/b]. This is a deal we’ll seal the only way we know how… [b]hellbinding[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/62886370218efc2875873e2c6c4318c312f67430.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Steam Deck Compatibility
notes.content:
[h3]Hi everyone! [/h3][p]Since the release of SkullX: Aibohphobia, we’ve received a couple questions regarding the game’s compatibility with Steam Deck, so we have decided to make this brief overview. [/p][p]SkullX: Aibohphobia was developed with controllers in mind, to provide the best user experience for every playstyle. Even before release, the game was [u]thoroughly tested and optimized for Steam Deck[/u] by our developers. 
[/p][h3]Here’s what you can expect when playing on Steam Deck: [/h3][list][*][p][b]Performance:[/b] The game runs at a stable 90 FPS, even on the highest settings. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Readability:[/b] The text and UI elements are fully readable and easily distinguishable on the display, both in the visual novel and combat parts of the game. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Smaller text:[/b] Some in-game writing pieces (mission brief file, notes) are meant to appear smaller on the screens for immersion. To simplify reading, we’ve added a zoom-in feature for those elements. Just use the stick to adjust the text size. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Resolution:[/b] Because of the nature of our hand-drawn art style, rescaling directly to 1280x800 was tricky. The game currently runs at 1280x720, resulting in slight letterboxing, so expect an artsy cinematic touch to your playthrough! [/p][/*][/list][h3]To conclude:[/h3][p]In our testing, SkullX: Aibohphobia performed great on Steam Deck, with image quality on par with PC and no technical setbacks.
[/p][p]However, if you run into any issues or want to share your Steam Deck playthrough experience, don’t hesitate to drop us a message on [url="https://discord.gg/2PQtDT23XB"]Discord[/url]. Feedback is greatly appreciated!
[/p][p]Thank you, and stay tuned for more updates! [/p]

notes.title: Launch Day
notes.content:
[p]Hey everyone, 

After over a year of blood, sweat, and therapy sessions, SkullX: Aibohphobia is finally live! It’s a choice-driven visual novel wrapped in hidden narrative layers, turn-based combat, and psychological horror. You’ll face off against your own reflection — literally — and decide who walks away. 

What to expect: [/p][list][*][p]A nonlinear story full of paranoia, branching paths, and secrets,[/p][/*][*][p]Tactical turn-based encounters,[/p][/*][*][p]Multiple endings — most of them regrettable,[/p][/*][*][p]Fully voice-acted inner demons,[/p][/*][*][p]A protagonist who may or may not be you,[/p][/*][/list][p]This is a weird one — built with love, pain, blood sacrifices, and way too many rewrites. We hope it stays with you long after the credits roll. 

Now go make some questionable decisions. 

– The SkullX and DSTRCT Creatives Team[/p]

notes.title: SkullX: Aibohphobia – New Release Date & Trailer
notes.content:
[p]Hey everyone,[/p][p]We’ve got a quick update:
[b]SkullX: Aibohphobia[/b] will now launch on [b]June 30th[/b] instead of late May. That’s just three more weeks—and in the meantime, we’ve prepared a brand new trailer to give you a deeper look at what’s coming:[/p][previewyoutube="dMNxdejLIVw;full"][/previewyoutube][hr][/hr][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/3465a9fa74c6bcc8d6903ac38af132cd90586d49.png"][/img][/p][p]The extra time gave us the chance to further flesh out key narrative arcs—and more importantly, lay the groundwork for how they’ll ripple through future chapters.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/fba821e0825d5f7ded82ea8f885440afca2fd9f3.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Aibohphobia[/b] is built around [i]hidden content[/i]—alternate branches, layered puzzles, and decisions that may seem small at first but can set off major narrative consequences later.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/af900a3c73360bb23368cf54c046a465ef6564a4.png"][/img][/p][p]Developing and weaving all of this together takes time, especially as it all ties directly into the structure of upcoming Chapters.[/p][hr][/hr][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/5265c79785fa4046ee1a01e48e46a1d1eb8cc63e.png"][/img][/p][p]Work on [b]Chapter 2[/b] is already underway.[/p][p]The choices you make—and the outcomes you reach—in Chapter 1 directly affect what happens next.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/bfe49359eef9f85f79654b2c4b4b97ed63123c47.png"][/img][/p][p]You won’t always see the consequences right away, but they’re there. And over time, the connections will become clearer. That’s where a lot of the game’s replayability—and surprises—come from.[/p][hr][/hr][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/a52bc80565d8945ff0689a19af6457efcc2a19e9.png"][/img][/p][p]We’re a small team focused almost entirely on development, so visibility is always a challenge.
If you’re excited about the game, [b]wishlist it[/b], [b]share the trailer[/b], or just send a link to a friend who might enjoy this kind of madness.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/0008ff99685e41970b80c5b95923aeddb2cfde27.png"][/img][/p][p]We’re almost there. Thanks for sticking with us! The experience will be worth the wait.[/p][p]– Team SkullX[/p]

notes.title: Announcing SkullX: Aibohphobia!
notes.content:
Welcome, Squad Leaders.

We’re thrilled to finally introduce our game to the world. A lot of blood, sweat, and tears went into it—some of which may or may not have been spilled during actual rituals.

[b]Here’s the announcement trailer, in case you missed it:[/b]

[previewyoutube=8lcoZ2D1Iiw;full][/previewyoutube]

If your first reaction is something like:
 “What the hell am I looking at?”
 “What is this game even about?”
 “What’s so scary about palindromes?”
 —then good. We’ve done our job.

I’m [b]Grim,[/b] the Project Lead of Aibohphobia, and I’d like to share how this project came to life—and what kind of experience awaits you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/dab38df83aa00411c411ac43cec2a990a1d0adc8.png[/img]

The world of Skullx was brought to life by our visionary artist, [b]Soh.[/b] Characterized by its distinctive dark art and skeletal inhabitants, this haunting realm laid the foundation for what would become [i]Aibophobia.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/50c2267840aaa35f362e2e315c98e7a63acedc1f.jpg[/img]

This world's setting has been taking shape since 2021, originally emerging as a collection of striking artwork. But as it began to draw attention, it became clear—there was more to this world than just cool designs. A deeper story was waiting to be told.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/1a0494076c885cc9e1888c1d8a38ed9f1f4acb8c.jpg[/img]

Something about Soh’s world wouldn’t let go of me. I kept turning it over in my mind, until I started building in it myself—small games at first, just experiments. Some of them are still floating around on itch.io.

They were passion projects, born from a love for the setting and its characters. But the response from those who stumbled upon them was way more positive than expected. Naturally, the next step was to go bigger: [b]build a proper visual novel grounded in this world.[/b]

But not just any visual novel.
We wanted it to be [i]occult[/i] in nature. At every level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/7e92cc8093b35664ec4f925894b06581a855e52b.png[/img]

The most important question we asked ourselves was:
[b]How should this game [i]feel?[/i][/b]
That broke down into four core things:
[list]
[*] How it [b]looks[/b]
[*] How it [b]reads[/b]
[*] How it [b]plays[/b]
[*] How it [b]sounds[/b]
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/df189c93396f1ffb734794bce7c5ff1512bd2cc1.png[/img]

We were lucky to have Soh join as [b]Art Director[/b] early on, just as we were exploring different styles. His input made all the difference.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/850606a6866a0a506fb0a3111708f9ceae290c2e.jpg[/img]

We eventually locked in a comic book art style inspired by [i]Mike Mignola[/i] and other legendary names in the field. Soh delivered the concept art, and our incredible illustrators brought those characters to life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/382fed08237ce5d115fc23126ae74aebe9af3352.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/0f38dc2b7e512b99ff4d36b3e45732b2bc0c4a1f.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/1cf7be24d85e9c5740e08e15b698ad1c9c3b2393.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/02d71d5759bfa7f0c53df830087a2582198a055e.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/8e36f34db4c8d4dc9a95fac6dc9dd494df8a1339.png[/img]

[i]Aibohphobia’s[/i] narrative is designed to reward attention and curiosity. It plays the long game: subtle hints, layered meaning, and revelations that don’t announce themselves. You’ll find traces of something larger in throwaway lines, background details, or moments that feel like coincidence—until they don’t.

That design approach was shaped by years of tabletop sessions with friends around the world. Our DM had a gift for planting seeds early and letting them bloom when you least expected. 

That same philosophy runs deep through this game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/8f14dd1b91119423c3d8e70b151049d2979989c4.jpg[/img]

[i]Aibohphobia[/i] is fully choice-driven, but no decision is ever strictly “wrong.” Some paths lead to revelations. Others lead to fortune. Or death. Or both. But none of them are boring.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/cf611f10a8c2626998d1bdfa1baf35bf45afc8ec.jpg[/img]

Story is the heart of this game. But it’s a story steeped in tension, violence, and chaos—so we needed gameplay that could carry all of that weight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/7778982a47be0e634eb2da11b76a2aa7a64f62fd.png[/img]

Enter our [b]custom-built turn-based combat system,[/b] inspired by games like [i]Darkest Dungeon, Iratus,[/i] and [i]Star Traders: Frontiers.[/i]
At least when it comes to mechanics.

But visually? We weren’t pulling from anything that existed. We knew exactly what we wanted: [b]a living comic book.[/b] That’s not something you can copy. We had to invent it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/49365ebb02cb9823ff6788e0a99095295aa80b87.jpg[/img]

Combat isn’t separate from the story.
The narrative keeps moving during fights. You’ll make choices mid-battle—and live with the consequences.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/e9f8cf86367b0a080f4ab38ce4cb82c0cd2354f4.jpg[/img]

The same goes for our point-and-click sequences. You’ll investigate scenes and objects to find answers… which usually lead to more questions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/ac8a1e5c3ba3df1f0d762f6e75d4c9137abd58bc.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/26c1ffb5b9c7343de9256d7b04d9cd16c87f1046.png[/img]

The music and sound design of Aibohphobia play a huge role in setting the tone. 

The process was… intense. We wanted to create more than just background noise; the music needed to be part of the experience—screeching, haunting, and bone-crushing when it mattered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/d74d4c6f5f1ae4115ac9648183279f3ccd3c9f0e.jpg[/img]

And, well, let’s just say we stopped asking how certain sounds were made. It’s probably safer that way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45583291/0c15f16c44290fb873fe7aea7f9b691183ce3cf8.png[/img]

[i]Aibohphobia[/i] is currently planned for release this May.

We’re still implementing a few tricky sequences and finalizing the voice work. More importantly, we’re running focused playtests to make sure the experience hits exactly how it should.

In the meantime, we’ll keep sharing updates, behind-the-scenes looks, and cursed glimpses of what’s to come.

Make sure to [b]wishlist the game[/b] if you haven’t already. 

And hey—stay away from palindromes. There’s always a reason to be afraid of them.
